title: Pear and chocolate cake
subtitle: a dense almond and chocolate cake with ripe pear halves sunk into the top
excerpt: Pear and chocolate is a classic French and Italian combination: the floral sweetness of ripe pear cuts through the richness of dark chocolate. The cake uses ground almonds in place of some of the flour, which gives a dense, fudgy crumb. The pear halves sit on the surface before baking and sink slightly into the batter as it rises.
sourceNotes: Pear and chocolate cake, a French and Italian-inspired combination widely adapted in British home baking. Method from contemporary British patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Ground almonds replace a portion of flour in some cake recipes to give a denser, moister crumb with a subtle nutty flavour. They are used in frangipane, financiers, and nut-meal cakes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 3 days. Serve at room temperature or very slightly warm.

content.text: instead of flour, making the cake naturally gluten free and giving it a dense, fudgy texture. Use ripe but firm pears (Conference or Comice work well). If the pears are very ripe they will soften completely into the cake; slightly firmer pears give more texture.

items.prepNote: peeled, halved, and cored (Conference or Comice)

content.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Grease and line a 23 cm round cake tin with baking parchment.
Melt the dark chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Remove from the heat and leave to cool slightly.
Beat the sugar and egg yolks together until pale and thickened, about 2 minutes. Stir in the cooled chocolate mixture. Fold in the ground almonds, cocoa powder, and baking powder.
Whisk the egg whites in a clean bowl to stiff peaks. Fold one-third into the chocolate batter to loosen it, then fold in the remaining whites in two more additions, keeping as much air as possible.

Pour into the prepared tin. Arrange the pear halves cut-side-down on the surface, pressing them in lightly. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the edges are set and a skewer inserted at the edge comes out clean. The centre will be slightly fudgy; that is correct. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes before removing.

attrs.problem: Pears sinking to the bottom of the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid placing pears on top of very thin batter; they need a batter with enough body to support them.
attrs.fix: Pat the pears dry with kitchen paper before placing them; excess moisture can make them drop faster.

attrs.problem: Cake collapsing in the centre when cooled
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven door before 35 minutes, and avoid under-baking.
attrs.fix: The centre will always be slightly softer than the edge due to the ground almonds and no flour structure. A completely flat collapse suggests the egg whites were over-folded; retain more air next time.
